name: Men-at-Arms
headerMeta: Heroic era · Melee infantry (Sword & Shield) · shields · 215 leadership · Honour Tree
pitch: A self-healing shield-and-sword line-holder whose entire kit runs through Cover Commander — cycle it every ~2s to keep its hidden damage-reduction passive up, and never V. It's the mandatory stepping stone to Paladins and folds fast to high-burst pressure, unable to hold a line the way top-tier T4 infantry can.

doctrines.name: Iron Damage Doctrine V
doctrines.note: Ironsides — replaceable with Epic Leadership Doctrine

veterancy.label: Top Line
veterancy.body: Amya: take if you can favorably help your unit (heavy armor, or fighting a medium-armor opponent) — rest Mid until 3/3 piercing dmg, rest non-selected line.

veterancy.label: Bottom Line
veterancy.body: Amya: take if you can't favorably help your unit (light armor, or vs medium such as musket) — rest Mid until 3/3 piercing dmg, rest non-selected line.

veterancy.label: Top Line
veterancy.body: KnightStalker's preferred line — slashing penetration, increased slashing dmg, crit-value penetration, shield-bash passive, block maintained while attacking, slashing defense in shield formation; doubles as the practice build for Paladins' innate trait.

veterancy.label: Middle Line
veterancy.body: Anti-ranged shield setup — block maintained while attacking, +120 block, +6 piercing dmg, reduced bleed on pierced armor, +80 additional block; pairs well with pikes.

veterancy.label: Bottom Line
veterancy.body: +3% HP, +6% slashing defense, +10% dmg in shield formation, 20% less ranged dmg in shield formation, 10% less rear-attack dmg, self-heal (~3,750 HP over 15s, ~1/3 of unit HP); capstone stun-immunity-in-shield-formation node called weak since heroes rarely use plain left-click for CC.

battleRole.positioning: Doctrines carry over on promotion to Paladins, so worth setting early even though this unit itself isn't strong. {2} Useful as a flanker, a temporary shield wall in front of pikes, or an opportunistic charger — not a line-holder. {2}
battleRole.formation: F3 (tight shield-plate) blocks ranged well: move to contact, hit V to concentrate fire, move in again, repeat — front-loads burst before spreading. {2} F2 (wider block) covers more frontage and suits charges, but is less effective than F3 funneling a chokepoint like a siege tower. {2} Open/Skirmish formation takes reduced ranged dmg — useful vs archers; press V to regroup overextended units. {2}
battleRole.tips: Cover Commander (order 2) is the best movement order before F3 unlocks — keeps formation compact, but the unit is aggressive and auto-engages, and won't disengage without explicit recall. {2} Reset Cover Commander every ~2s: the hidden dmg-reduction passive decays from 40% to 0% over 4-6s. {1}{2} Charging in tight shield formation concentrates hits on a small area — effective vs heroes, but doesn't reliably solo-kill one; more effective wiping lighter unshielded units. {2} Forgetting to press V after contact overcharges and can lose ~half the unit's strength. {2}

cards.name: Berserkers

cards.name: Paladins

cards.name: Stalwarts
cards.why: cited alongside Berserkers/Paladins as top-tier T4 infantry that can hold a line where MAA can't; also shown countering an MAA back-charge via block-while-attacking

matchups.pressure: You pressure: Low-tier units relying on hit-to-debuff, and heroes. {1} Charging into Berserkers is comparatively safe — blunt favors the charger. {2}

controls.notes: Always fight in Cover Commander mode, never V — Cover Commander is the main DPS tool. {1} Charging in (no V/X-move) before Cover Commander stacks a mini-charge on the next impact; mini-charge cooldown in Cover Commander mode is 9 seconds. {1} Can charge to engage, but it's often better to simply activate Cover Commander and move in and out of combat. {1} Reset Cover Commander roughly every 2 seconds — a hidden passive gives dmg reduction that decays from 40% to 0% over 4-6s if not refreshed. {1}{2}
